hard_gates.evidence: The frame begins around the operator's mid-torso and ends above the helmet; legs and full-body locomotion are absent.
The circular bore is centered toward the viewer, with the enlarged muzzle, optic, and face stacked along one immediately readable axis.
The muzzle supplies the first-glance hook, the optic carries the eye backward, and the unobscured face provides the second focal plane.
The operator visibly shoulders the compact carbine and holds the barrel directly along the camera axis in a braced aiming posture.
Both eyes, nose, lips, and jaw remain readable around and above the optic despite strong weapon foreshortening.
The result retains an unmistakably adult facial impression, natural skin detail, and mature head-to-torso proportions without visible de-aging or dollification.

Side-by-side inspection retains the long oval face, almond eye aperture and spacing, straight slender nose, full lower lip, soft jaw width, and long dark wavy hair; helmet pressure and aiming tension account for minor variation.
The forward glove wraps the handguard and the rear glove occupies the receiver and grip area; wrists and forearms connect coherently to the shoulders with no obvious extra hand.
Bore, muzzle device, handguard, receiver, optic, and cheek line remain aligned under the intended foreshortening without a duplicated barrel or disconnected sight.
Rain beads across helmet and uniform, warm rim light catches wet edges, and the blurred concrete compound shares the same cool storm exposure.

Modern helmet and communications gear, plate carrier, disciplined weapon carriage, Republic of Korea flag patch, rain, and campaign lighting support the requested Armed Forces promotional-poster look.

The Korean flag and hangar-style Korean lettering in the background are generated scene dressing and were not independently verified as official wording or design.
